title: Tool signature manifest and validation playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a compact 'tool signature manifest' that complements full JSON Schema for runtime tool/function calling. Goal: make authoring clearer for integrators, make runtime validation deterministic, and provide actionable remediations to calling clients. The manifest is an opinionated, minimal authoring format (markdown-like fields + canonical types) that maps to full JSON Schema for machine validation but is optimized for humans and for runtime quick checks. It should support: explicit parameter versions, stability hints (stable/experimental/deprecated), coercion guidance (coerceStringToNumber: true/false), deterministic discriminator rules, and a small canonical error vocabulary for client UX. This ticket defines the manifest shape (human-friendly), canonical error codes and messages, recommended validation modes (strict | permissive | compat), telemetry events, and a runtime ergonomics playbook for SDKs. The manifest is not meant to replace full schema but to reduce authoring errors and ambiguity that lead to high customer support load.
acceptance_criteria: A compact manifest spec (<= 1 A4) that maps 1:1 to a validation pipeline and example translation to JSON Schema
A canonical error code list with recommended HTTP mapping and client-facing message templates
Design doc + SDK adapter PR that demonstrates permissive and strict modes with example tool definitions
Runtime emits telemetry events for validation_reject and validation_coerce with sample payloads
Backward-compatible fallback: tools without manifest must still be callable via legacy schema with a warning telemetry event
decisions: Two authored validation modes: 'strict' (default for Dedicated/Private) and 'compat' (permissive, for hosted PLG) to balance safety and friction.
Canonical error codes prefix: TS- (Tool Signature). Use short machine codes and a localization-friendly message template.
Manifest will include a 'coercion' hint per field: allowed values are 'none', 'coerce', 'try_coerce'. The runtime will only auto-coerce in 'compat' mode and emit telemetry when it does.
We will publish a small reference SDK adapter (python/node) that demonstrates error-to-UX mapping and suggested client messages.
implementation_notes: Prototype translation: runtime module tools/manifest_translator (PR linked below)
Add telemetry events: validation.rejected, validation.coerced, validation.fallback_used. Include tool_key, caller_id, error_code, and short schema fingerprint in payloads.
Schema fingerprint: use sha256 of canonical JSON Schema bloom to detect schema drift between authoring and runtime.
SDKs: add a client-side preflight check that can run 'manifest-lint' to catch authoring mistakes before runtime calls.

example_manifest_snippet:
---
name: create_invoice
version: 1.0.0
description: Create an invoice for a customer with itemized lines
parameters:
  - name: customer_id
    type: string
    required: true
    stability: stable
  - name: total_amount
    type: number
    required: true
    coercion: try_coerce
  - name: lines
    type: array
    items: object
    required: true
    discriminator: item_type
---
canonical_errors: TS-VAL-001: missing_required - Required parameter missing. Client hint: add parameter '<param_name>'
TS-VAL-002: type_mismatch - Type mismatch for '<param_name>'. Client hint: expected <type>, received <type>. Suggest: coerce string to number only in compat mode.
TS-VAL-003: unknown_param - Unrecognized parameter '<param_name>'. Client hint: remove or migrate to latest manifest.
TS-VAL-004: coercion_failed - Attempted coercion failed for '<param_name>'. Client hint: normalize input upstream.
TS-VAL-005: validation_timeout - Validation exceeded allowed time budget. Client hint: split payload or register as bulk operation.
TS-VAL-006: ambiguous_discriminator - Discriminator resolution ambiguous for '<param_name>'. Client hint: add explicit 'type' field or update manifest discriminator rules.
TS-VAL-007: deprecated_param_used - Parameter '<param_name>' is deprecated. Client hint: migrate to '<replacement_param>'
backward_compatibility_plan: If manifest is missing, runtime falls back to legacy JSON Schema validation and emits telemetry validation.fallback_used.
Start with a soft rollout: hosted PLG clusters will enable 'compat' mode for 30 days to gather telemetry, then warn authors to adopt manifest semantics.
Provide a lint tool 'manifest-lint --check-compat' that flags coercions and deprecated usage and suggests fixes.
